acceptance: A UAT retry is admitted only when the remaining job budget covers the cell limit plus the outside-kill margin.
context: Noted by the UAT-cells implementer in the run-timeout effort (#4437).
description:
## Problem
`tests/uat/infrastructure_retry.py` (`with_infrastructure_retry`) retries a cell when `remaining_s >= timeout_s`. Since #4437 a cell can run until `timeout_s + OUTSIDE_KILL_MARGIN_S` (60 s) before the runner kills it, so a retry admitted with exactly `timeout_s` left can overrun the job budget by up to 60 seconds.

## Change
Compare the remaining budget with the cell's worst-case duration (`outside_limit_s(timeout_s)` in tests/uat/runner.py).

## Decision gates
No change to cell limits, the 60-second margin, which cells retry, or pass/fail rules (owner decisions, run-timeout-uat-cells-20261120). Retry counting for `hung` stays identical to `timed-out`.

## Verification rubric
A test (fails before) with a fake clock where remaining is between `timeout_s` and `timeout_s + 60`: the retry is skipped as insufficient time; one where remaining exceeds it: the retry runs. `make pr-preflight` exits 0.

## Guardrails
Work in a linked worktree (`make worktree-create`), never the primary clone. Edit files with the edit tool, never by script. Heavy work (benchmarks, test tiers, UAT, generators at scale) only through `make heavy-run` or lock-taking entry points; never skip the lock, admission or watchdog; never delete anything under `~/Developer/benchmark_runs`. No live cloud run and no cloud credentials unless this item's Decision gates say the owner approved it in the current task. BenchBox imposes no default run limit: add none. No comments or docstrings in first-party code; one changelog fragment for a user-facing change. Never post a stand-in review, close and reopen a pull request to restart CI, use `--no-verify`, force-push, or rewrite an author. Arm once; a second time only after fixing the cause the refusal named. Reply on every review thread; resolve it only after the bot's review of the new head does not raise it again.
